sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_f.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Base comp itself isn't a fraud signal — the question is whether total comp (base + bonus + deferred + nontaxable + related-org) is reasonable for the role. Outlier base compensation, especially in small orgs, is the visible signal that warrants attention.
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_f.what_a_high_rate_means: Sectors with high median base comp reflect sector pay scales (Health Care executives, university presidents); not fraud-adjacent on its own.
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_f.what_a_low_rate_means: Below-market base comp often correlates with founder-CEO arrangements where comp is delivered through related entities or non-W-2 channels.
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_f.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion has lower median base comp than most secular sectors; the gap is partly real (smaller orgs) and partly structural (§107 housing allowance excluded from base). Median-comp distribution by sector not separately tabulated here.
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_f.subgroup_caveats: Always control for org size before comparing comp medians.

sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_r.what_it_is: Base salary paid by a RELATED organization (Sched R entity).
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_r.statutory_basis: Reportable on the filing-org's Sched J under Form 990 instructions; FMV/aggregation analysis under Reg. §53.4958-4(b)(1)(i).
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_r.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: The 'paid through related LLC' disclosure-avoidance pattern. Officer total comp aggregates across filing-org and related-org; the related-org column is where comp paid through a captive subsidiary appears. Cross-reference with Sched R to identify which entity is paying. The Grassley inquiry specifically named this pattern as a disclosure-avoidance technique.
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_r.what_a_high_rate_means: Concentration of comp in the related-org column relative to filing-org column flags the 'paid through related entity' pattern.
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_r.what_a_low_rate_means: Most officer comp is paid by the filing org; absence is the baseline.
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_r.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion's largest broadcast-ministry filers concentrate related-org comp via book-publishing and broadcasting LLCs; secular Health Care concentrates it via subsidiary medical groups. Related-org comp distribution by sector not separately tabulated here.
sched_j_compensation.base_compensation_r.subgroup_caveats: Health Care (E) and Education (B) have legitimate sector-structural reasons; cross-reference is required.

sched_j_compensation.bonus_filing_org.what_it_is: Bonus / incentive comp from the filing org.
sched_j_compensation.bonus_filing_org.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Bonus comp ratio (bonus / base) is itself diagnostic — ratios above 30% are unusual outside of physician-productivity contexts. Where bonuses are large and contingent on revenue or net earnings, the Sched J Pt I contingent flags become the analytical anchor.
sched_j_compensation.bonus_filing_org.what_a_high_rate_means: Sectors with high bonus-to-base ratios warrant cross-reference with the contingent-pay flags.
sched_j_compensation.bonus_filing_org.what_a_low_rate_means: Salary-only structures are simpler and lower-risk.
sched_j_compensation.bonus_filing_org.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion has materially lower bonus prevalence; theological objections to performance-based ministry pay are common. The contingent-comp comparison (secular ~7.9× religion) is the closest measured proxy.
sched_j_compensation.bonus_filing_org.subgroup_caveats: Health Care dominates secular bonus distribution per regulatory framing.

sched_j_compensation.bonus_related_org.what_it_is: Bonus / incentive comp from a related org.
sched_j_compensation.bonus_related_org.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Same disclosure-avoidance concern as base from related org — bonus paid through an affiliate keeps the filing-org Pt VII comp number low.
sched_j_compensation.bonus_related_org.what_a_high_rate_means: Concentration here flags the related-entity comp-routing pattern.
sched_j_compensation.bonus_related_org.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion's broadcast-ministry subset and secular Health Care subsidiaries account for most cases per regulatory framing. Not separately tabulated here.

sched_j_compensation.other_filing_org.what_it_is: Other reportable comp from the filing org (commissions, taxable fringe, etc.).
sched_j_compensation.other_filing_org.statutory_basis: W-2 box 1 inclusion regime under Reg. §1.61-21.
sched_j_compensation.other_filing_org.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Large 'other' comp relative to base flags either substantial taxable fringe (housing, vehicle, club dues reported as comp) or one-time payments (severance, signing bonus). Read with the corresponding Sched J Pt I perk flags.
sched_j_compensation.other_filing_org.what_a_high_rate_means: Sectors with high 'other' shares warrant Sched J Pt I cross-reference.
sched_j_compensation.other_filing_org.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion may have higher 'other' share at smaller filers because non-W-2 benefits (housing, ministry vehicle) appear here when properly reported. Distribution not separately tabulated here.
sched_j_compensation.other_filing_org.subgroup_caveats: Read by ratio to base, not absolute level.

sched_j_compensation.deferred_compensati.what_it_is: Deferred comp set aside by the filing org.
sched_j_compensation.deferred_compensati.statutory_basis: IRC §457(b)/(f) for tax-exempts; §409A general nonqualified deferred comp rules.
sched_j_compensation.deferred_compensati.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Deferred comp itself is normal; large accumulated balances become outsized excess-benefit exposure if comp committee documentation is weak. The Sched J Pt I supplemental_nonqualified_retirement flag is the structural antecedent.
sched_j_compensation.deferred_compensati.what_a_high_rate_means: Concentration in larger orgs and in Health Care / Education executive comp.
sched_j_compensation.deferred_compensati.what_a_low_rate_means: Smaller orgs don't fund deferred comp meaningfully.
sched_j_compensation.deferred_compensati.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: secular substantially higher; reflects executive labor-market structure. Deferred-comp distribution by sector not separately tabulated here.

sched_j_compensation.deferred_compensati.what_it_is: Deferred comp set aside by a related org.
sched_j_compensation.deferred_compensati.statutory_basis: Same as filing-org deferred; aggregated for §4958-4(b) reasonableness analysis.
sched_j_compensation.deferred_compensati.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Same disclosure-routing concern as base/bonus from related org.

sched_j_compensation.nontaxable_benefits.what_it_is: Non-taxable benefits provided by the filing org (health insurance, qualified retirement contributions, etc.).
sched_j_compensation.nontaxable_benefits.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Mostly benign; large non-taxable benefits in small orgs warrant a quick check that the items are actually qualifying (e.g., is the 'health insurance' a self-funded reimbursement masquerading as a qualified plan?).
sched_j_compensation.nontaxable_benefits.what_a_high_rate_means: High median non-taxable benefits correlate with org size and benefit-plan sophistication.
sched_j_compensation.nontaxable_benefits.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: secular larger orgs lead; religion has narrower distribution. Not separately tabulated here.

sched_j_compensation.total_filing_org.what_it_is: Total reportable + other comp from the filing org.
sched_j_compensation.total_filing_org.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: The headline comp number. Outlier total comp in small orgs is the most visible single signal of insider extraction. High-end clusters are concentrated in expected sectors (Health Care, large Education); positives outside those clusters are diagnostic.
sched_j_compensation.total_filing_org.what_a_high_rate_means: Sectors with high median total comp reflect sector pay scales; not inherently fraud-adjacent.
sched_j_compensation.total_filing_org.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion has lower median (smaller orgs); religion's right tail concentrates in religiously-sponsored hospital systems (NTEE-E hospitals owned by religious sponsoring entities such as Ascension, Trinity Health, Providence, CommonSpirit). Compensation-distribution medians by sector not separately tabulated in this revision's data inputs.
sched_j_compensation.total_filing_org.subgroup_caveats: Right-tail comp in religion is dominated by hospital systems with religious sponsorship; the sponsoring church-status entity often does not appear in this comp tail.

sched_j_compensation.total_related_org.statutory_basis: Aggregated for §4958-4(b) reasonableness analysis across the controlled group.
sched_j_compensation.total_related_org.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Total related-org comp ≥ filing-org comp is the most concentrated form of the 'paid through related entity' disclosure-avoidance pattern.
sched_j_compensation.total_related_org.what_a_high_rate_means: Concentration warrants cross-reference with Sched R.
sched_j_compensation.total_related_org.what_a_low_rate_means: Officers paid only by the filing org are the baseline.
sched_j_compensation.total_related_org.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: secular Health Care system executives often have substantial related-org comp from parent and sister entities; religion's broadcast-ministry CEOs have related-org comp from publishing/media LLCs. Distribution not separately tabulated here.

sched_j_compensation.title.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Title concentration (most comp going to a single FOUNDER/PRESIDENT/CEO) is the structural signal of founder-dominated comp architecture. Truncated at ~12 chars in some IRS schema versions ('VICE PRESIDE,' 'EXECUTIVE DI').
sched_j_compensation.title.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: regulatory framing predicts religion title vocabulary leans toward PASTOR/MINISTER/FOUNDER and secular toward CEO/PRESIDENT/EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR. Title-text distribution has not been mined here.

part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_o.what_it_is: W-2 box 1 / 1099 box 7 reportable comp from the filing org. 87% of rows are $0 (uncompensated board members).
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_o.statutory_basis: Form 990 Part VII Section A; W-2 box 1.
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_o.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Outlier compensation in this column is the most public single signal in the entire 990. Cross-org comp (same person, multiple EINs, same year) is the related signal that surfaces shared-insider architectures.
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_o.what_a_high_rate_means: Sector pay scales dominate the median; outliers in small-org sectors are the diagnostic positives.
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_o.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Filter to >0 before computing medians; raw means are dominated by zero-comp board members. Sector medians not separately tabulated here.
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_o.subgroup_caveats: Hypothesis: Health Care (E) dominates the right tail; religion right tail concentrates in religiously-sponsored hospital systems coded NTEE-E rather than NTEE-X.

part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_r.what_it_is: Reportable comp from a related organization (Sched R entity).
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_r.statutory_basis: Same as filing-org reportable comp; aggregated under §4958-4(b).
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_r.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Insider drawing comp from a related entity is the structural antecedent of the 'paid through related LLC' disclosure-avoidance pattern. Cross-reference with Sched R Pt II/IV to identify the paying affiliate.
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_r.what_a_high_rate_means: Concentration of officers with substantial related-org comp warrants Sched R cross-reference.
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_r.what_a_low_rate_means: Most officers are paid only by the filing org.
part_vii_officers.reportable_comp_from_r.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: pattern is more salient in the religion-corpus broadcast-ministry subset and the secular-corpus health-system subset. Not separately tabulated here.

part_vii_officers.other_compensation.what_it_is: Other comp from the filing org (deferred, benefits, etc.).
part_vii_officers.other_compensation.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Same as Sched J other_filing_org but at Pt VII granularity. Where other comp dwarfs reportable comp, taxable fringe or one-time payments dominate.
part_vii_officers.other_compensation.what_a_high_rate_means: Sectors with high other-to-reportable ratios warrant Sched J Pt I perk cross-reference.
part_vii_officers.other_compensation.what_a_low_rate_means: Most officers have low other comp.
part_vii_officers.other_compensation.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion may have higher other-comp share at smaller filers (housing, vehicle, ministry travel reported here when correctly handled). Not separately tabulated here.
part_vii_officers.other_compensation.subgroup_caveats: Cross-reference with Sched J Pt I.

part_vii_officers.average_hours.what_it_is: Average hours per week the person works for the filing org.
part_vii_officers.average_hours.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Officer with extremely low average hours but substantial comp is the no-show-officer pattern. Especially diagnostic when combined with cross-EIN appearances (same person, multiple orgs, low hours at each).
part_vii_officers.average_hours.what_a_high_rate_means: Median hours ≥ 40 indicates full-time officer roles; <5 indicates board-only positions.
part_vii_officers.average_hours.what_a_low_rate_means: Volunteer-board hours are usually 1–2 per week.
part_vii_officers.average_hours.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion has a higher share of pastor-as-officer at ≥40 hours; secular has a higher share of non-executive directors at 1–2 hours. Hours distribution not separately tabulated here.
part_vii_officers.average_hours.subgroup_caveats: Cross-reference with reportable_comp_from_org to detect comp/hours anomalies.

part_vii_officers.individual_trustee_or_.what_it_is: True = serves as individual trustee or director.
part_vii_officers.individual_trustee_or_.statutory_basis: Form 990 Pt VII Section A role classification.
part_vii_officers.individual_trustee_or_.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Role classification itself is not a fraud signal. Useful for filtering to governing-body members for board-independence ratio analysis.
part_vii_officers.individual_trustee_or_.what_a_high_rate_means: High share indicates a large governing body.
part_vii_officers.individual_trustee_or_.what_a_low_rate_means: Small board with concentrated officer roles.
part_vii_officers.individual_trustee_or_.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion has smaller average board size; secular boards are larger. Board-size distribution not separately tabulated here.

part_vii_officers.officer.what_it_is: True = is an officer of the org (President, Treasurer, Secretary, CEO, etc.).
part_vii_officers.officer.statutory_basis: Form 990 Pt VII Section A role classification.
part_vii_officers.officer.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Officer role classification triggers Sched J inclusion at the over-$150k comp threshold. Useful for filtering analyses to compensation-bearing roles.
part_vii_officers.officer.what_a_high_rate_means: High share suggests many compensated leadership roles.
part_vii_officers.officer.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion has higher per-org officer counts when pastoral staff are designated officers; secular varies by sector. Per-org officer counts not separately tabulated here.

part_vii_officers.key_employee.what_it_is: True = key employee (over the $150k/$210k thresholds plus other tests under Form 990 instructions).
part_vii_officers.key_employee.statutory_basis: Form 990 Pt VII Section A; per-year inflation-adjusted thresholds.
part_vii_officers.key_employee.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Key-employee designation expands the rebuttable-presumption reach to non-officer high earners under §4958-3(c). Sectors with many key employees have broader §4958 exposure surface.
part_vii_officers.key_employee.what_a_low_rate_means: Smaller orgs rarely have key employees.
part_vii_officers.key_employee.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: secular has materially more key-employee disclosures than religion because of org-size differences. Distribution not separately tabulated here.

part_vii_officers.highest_compensated_em.what_it_is: True = one of the top-5 highest-paid employees not otherwise listed.
part_vii_officers.highest_compensated_em.statutory_basis: Form 990 Pt VII Section A; reportable if comp ≥ $100k.
part_vii_officers.highest_compensated_em.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Disclosure category itself isn't a fraud signal. Useful for analyzing whether the top-5 includes family members or vendors that should appear elsewhere.
part_vii_officers.highest_compensated_em.what_a_low_rate_means: Smaller orgs don't have $100k+ non-officer employees.
part_vii_officers.highest_compensated_em.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: secular has structurally more entries; religion's entries cluster in larger broadcast and hospital-system filers. Distribution not separately tabulated here.

part_vii_officers.former.what_it_is: True = former officer/director/key employee still receiving reportable comp during the year.
part_vii_officers.former.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Former-employee continued comp is normal in severance and deferred-comp contexts; the diagnostic question is amount relative to original role and whether the arrangement was pre-approved with comparability data. Large continuing payments to founders post-separation are the watch list.
part_vii_officers.former.what_a_high_rate_means: Rare across the corpus; positives are individually diagnostic.
part_vii_officers.former.what_a_low_rate_means: Most orgs don't have former-officer ongoing comp.
part_vii_officers.former.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion has visible former-founder cases; secular has more former-CEO severance-tail cases. Distribution not separately tabulated here.
part_vii_officers.former.subgroup_caveats: Read individual rows, not aggregate rates.

part_vii_contractors.compensation.what_it_is: Compensation paid to a top-5 contractor (>$100k).
part_vii_contractors.compensation.statutory_basis: Form 990 Pt VII Section B; required disclosure for top-5 contractors over $100k.
part_vii_contractors.compensation.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Contractor comp itself isn't a fraud signal. The diagnostic angle is whether the contractor is also an interested person under §4958 — cross-reference contractor name against Sched L Pt IV vendor list and Sched R related-entity list.
part_vii_contractors.compensation.what_a_high_rate_means: Large contractor payments warrant cross-reference with Sched L Pt IV.
part_vii_contractors.compensation.what_a_low_rate_means: Smaller orgs don't trigger the $100k threshold.
part_vii_contractors.compensation.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis: religion has narrower contractor populations; secular Health Care has very wide ones because of sector size. Distribution not separately tabulated here.

part_vii_contractors.contractor_state.what_it_is: Contractor US state or foreign country.
part_vii_contractors.contractor_state.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Contractor location alone isn't a fraud signal. Cross-state contractor concentration with named insider connections is.
part_vii_contractors.contractor_state.what_a_high_rate_means: Concentration in same state as filer is normal.
part_vii_contractors.contractor_state.what_a_low_rate_means: Wide geographic dispersion is normal in larger filers.

part_vii_contractors.services_descriptio.why_it_signals_fraud_or_misappropriation: Read by content. Vague descriptions ('management services,' 'consulting') for substantial-dollar contracts warrant cross-reference with Sched L Pt IV vendor list.
part_vii_contractors.services_descriptio.how_to_compare_religion_vs_secular: Hypothesis (not measured in this corpus): regulatory framing predicts religion contractor descriptions skew toward broadcasting/media-production/construction vocabulary while secular skews toward IT/construction/consulting/legal. Description-text mining has not been performed here.

comparison_pairs.label: Religion (X) vs Education (B)
comparison_pairs.rationale: Education is the largest secular major: 185,568 filings (2014-2024), or 194,778 including partial-2025. Shares with religion a high mission-driven non-commercial posture, founder-or-family-led structures at the small end (private schools), and substantial use of campus housing for staff. Both populate §170(b)(1)(A)(i)/(ii) public-charity status but face very different regulatory environments.
comparison_pairs.interpretive_warning: Education's per-filing Sched J Pt I rate (26.77%) is roughly 2.9× religion's (9.23%) — control for org size before reading the gap as religion-specific. Conversely, religion's §107 housing exclusion makes raw housing-allowance rates non-comparable; religion's elevated rate here is statutory, not behavioral.
comparison_pairs.what_to_conclude: Religion has materially weaker procedural comp-governance disclosure than Education on the visible Sched J Pt I axis; whether this survives org-size control is a separate question.
comparison_pairs.what_not_to_conclude: Do not infer Education is 'cleaner' from raw rates; Education has substantially more Pt IV business transactions (7.20% vs religion 4.83%) and substantially more Sched R Pt II related-tax-exempt density (20.91% vs religion 9.27%).

comparison_pairs.label: Religion (X) vs Health Care (E)
comparison_pairs.rationale: Health Care has the highest related-party transaction density in the dataset across multiple Schedules: Pt IV business transactions 11.38%, Sched R Pt V transactions 26.52%, Sched J Pt I 55.65%, Sched R Pt II related tax-exempt 48.60%. Religion's per-filing rates are far below all four (4.83%, 5.20%, 9.23%, 9.27%). The driver is sector-structural: physician-practice and system-affiliate architecture. Health Care n=96,633 filings (2014-2024).
comparison_pairs.interpretive_warning: Catholic, Adventist, Baptist, and Mennonite hospital systems are classified NTEE-E in this dataset, not NTEE-X. The 'religiously-sponsored health system' phenomenon is excluded from the religion corpus by NTEE coding even though sponsoring entities exercise governance control. This is the most consequential coding boundary in the comparison.
comparison_pairs.what_to_conclude: Religion's lower rates on every Health Care-dominant field are partly a coding artifact — the religious health-system activity has moved into the secular corpus by NTEE classification.
comparison_pairs.what_not_to_conclude: Do not read Health Care's high Pt IV / Sched R rates as evidence of more fraud; sector-structural physician-practice and system-affiliate relationships drive the bulk of these positives.

comparison_pairs.label: Religion (X) vs Human Services (P)
comparison_pairs.rationale: Human Services is the second-largest sector: 171,347 filings (2014-2024) — 176,886 including partial-2025. Most directly comparable to religion in mission orientation — direct-service provision, often community-based, often founder-led at the small end. P has heavy faith-based-program-but-not-coded-X overlap (Catholic Charities, Lutheran Services, Jewish Family Service affiliates).
comparison_pairs.interpretive_warning: The largest 'religion-affiliated' service providers (Catholic Charities USA network, Lutheran Services in America affiliates, Jewish Federation affiliates) are NTEE-P, not NTEE-X. The religion-vs-P comparison is therefore not 'religious' vs 'secular' but 'pastoral / theological' vs 'faith-affiliated service.' P's §4958 rate is 0.0286% (49 of 171,347) vs religion 0.0578% (50 of 86,455) — religion is roughly 2× P despite organizational overlap.
comparison_pairs.what_to_conclude: Religion (pastoral) and Human Services (service-delivery, including faith-affiliated) have meaningfully different fraud-relevant disclosure patterns despite overlapping social positioning.
comparison_pairs.what_not_to_conclude: Do not conflate NTEE-P with 'non-religious' — a substantial fraction of P is faith-affiliated service organizations.

comparison_pairs.label: Religion (X) vs Philanthropy & Voluntarism (T)
comparison_pairs.rationale: Philanthropy 58,410 filings (2014-2024) — 60,206 with partial-2025. Includes public-charity foundations operating as 501(c)(3) public charities (filing Form 990, not 990-PF), donor-advised-fund sponsors, and federated giving organizations. T has the highest 509(a)(3) supporting-org share among secular majors — the same regulatory regime that captures many religiously-sponsored supporting orgs (denominational endowments, mission funds).
comparison_pairs.interpretive_warning: Religion's supporting-org subset (denominational endowments, missionary fund-holders) maps closely to T's foundation-affiliate structure. Direct rate comparison across X and T captures the 509(a)(3) governance regime as much as the religious/secular distinction.
comparison_pairs.what_to_conclude: T's per-filing Sched R Pt II rate (29.03%) is ~3.1× religion's (9.27%); the gap reflects foundation-affiliate architecture rather than fraud.
comparison_pairs.what_not_to_conclude: Do not infer foundations have more insider dealing from elevated Sched R rates; the disclosure rate reflects affiliate-architecture density, not behavior.

comparison_pairs.label: Religion (X) vs Housing & Shelter (L)
comparison_pairs.rationale: Housing & Shelter 77,132 filings (2014-2024) — 79,712 with partial-2025. Has the highest Sched R Pt II rate in the entire dataset (52.18%) because each property is typically held in a separate LLC for liability reasons. Housing also leads Sched R Pt V at 20.80%. Religion's parsonage-and-real-estate subset shares some of this architecture but at much lower density (9.27% Sched R Pt II, 5.20% Sched R Pt V).
comparison_pairs.interpretive_warning: Housing's elevated rates on every Sched R field are structural — LIHTC and HUD-financed housing requires separate-entity-per-project for tax-credit and lender purposes. None of this is fraud-adjacent.
comparison_pairs.what_to_conclude: Housing is the clearest example of why disclosure-density does not equal fraud-density; the comparison shows religion's structural simplicity, not religion's relative cleanliness.
comparison_pairs.what_not_to_conclude: Do not use Housing's elevated rates as a fraud baseline.

comparison_pairs.label: Religion (X) vs Mental Health & Crisis (F)
comparison_pairs.rationale: Mental Health & Crisis 28,772 filings (2014-2024) — 29,726 with partial-2025. The only secular major where the §4958 excess-benefit admission rate (0.1112%, 32 of 28,772) exceeds religion's (0.0578%, 50 of 86,455). F leads the entire 24-major leaderboard and is the only sector ranked above religion on this metric. F is dominated by smaller community mental-health providers, crisis-line operators, and founder-led counseling centers — structurally similar to small religious orgs in founder-dependence.
comparison_pairs.interpretive_warning: F is structurally similar to small religious orgs in founder-dependence and small-board governance; the elevated §4958 rate likely reflects shared structural risk, not sector-specific behavior.
comparison_pairs.what_to_conclude: Religion is not uniquely high on §4958 admissions; founder-dominated small orgs across sectors share the pattern. Religion ranks #2 of 24 on §4958 disclosure rate; F is #1.
comparison_pairs.what_not_to_conclude: Do not treat religion as the only sector with elevated excess-benefit risk; F is higher under the post-audit disclose-rate construction.

comparison_pairs.label: Religion (X) vs International, Foreign Affairs (Q)
comparison_pairs.rationale: International 32,910 filings (2014-2024) — 33,622 with partial-2025. Overlaps substantially with religion in mission posture (faith-based foreign missions are often classified Q, not X). Q has the most legitimate offshore-domicile activity of any major. Direct comparison helps separate 'religion' from 'foreign-missionary' as analytic categories.
comparison_pairs.interpretive_warning: Major faith-based foreign-mission organizations (Samaritan's Purse, World Vision US, Compassion International, etc.) are classified Q, not X. Religion-X corpus captures domestic religious orgs preferentially.
comparison_pairs.what_to_conclude: Q is the secular major most affected by the NTEE coding boundary with religion.
comparison_pairs.what_not_to_conclude: Do not infer that 'religious organizations don't do international work' from the X/Q split — they do, and most of it is in Q.

comparison_pairs.label: Religion (X) vs Community Improvement (S)
comparison_pairs.rationale: Community Improvement 78,731 filings (2014-2024) — 81,133 with partial-2025. Covers chambers of commerce, business-improvement districts, neighborhood associations, and community development corps. S has the lowest §4958 admission rate among substantial majors (0.0102%, 8 of 78,731) — useful as a low-baseline comparator. Religion (0.0578%) is roughly 5.7× S.
comparison_pairs.interpretive_warning: S has heavy 501(c)(4)/(c)(6) co-presence in related entities (the business-association ecosystem), unlike religion which co-presents with (c)(2) and (c)(3) only per regulatory framing. Different ecosystem, different baseline.
comparison_pairs.what_to_conclude: S is the clearest 'low-baseline secular' comparator for excess-benefit rates.
comparison_pairs.what_not_to_conclude: Do not treat S as 'normal nonprofit' — it has its own structural features (business-association ecosystem, chamber-of-commerce comp practices).

comparison_pairs.label: Religion (X) vs Arts, Culture & Humanities (A)
comparison_pairs.rationale: Arts 108,296 filings (2014-2024) — 112,428 with partial-2025. Third-largest sector and most resembles religion in its concentration of small founder-led orgs with high-passion donor bases (parallel to religious congregations with founder-pastors). A leads the dataset on insider-loan disclosure rate (4.89%), narrowly above religion (4.70%) — religion ranks #2 of 24 on this metric.
comparison_pairs.interpretive_warning: Arts' high insider-loan rate is hypothesized to be dominated by founder-bankrolling-the-organization (loan_to_organization direction), not org-to-insider extraction, per regulatory framing. Direction matters here; the direction-split has not been quantified in current data.
comparison_pairs.what_to_conclude: Religion's insider-loan rate is virtually tied with Arts; the founder-bankrolling pattern is shared in regulatory framing.
comparison_pairs.what_not_to_conclude: Do not treat Arts' high loan rate as a fraud signal without checking loan_to_organization direction.

X.label: Religion-related
X.what_this_sector_is: Religious congregations and denominational entities that voluntarily file Form 990 (§6033(a)(3)(A)(i) exempts churches; this corpus is the opt-in subset, mostly ECFA members, federal-grant recipients, and religious nonprofits coded as church-status). 86,455 filings, 17,870 EINs (2014-2024 excl partial-2025); 88,660 filings, 18,017 EINs including 2025.
X.typical_related_party_profile: Founder-pastor governance is common; smaller average board size; less professionalized comp governance per regulatory framing; §107 housing allowance structurally distinct; broadcasting-ministry corporate families create concentrated Sched R networks for the small subset of large filers.
fields_where_this_sector_is_notable: sched_l_excess_benefit (per-filing 0.0578%, 2.19× secular, ranks #2 of 24 — F leads at 0.1112%)
sched_l_loans (per-filing 4.70%, ranks #2 of 24 — A leads at 4.89%)
sched_l_loans.written_agreement (conditional unwritten share 39.9% vs secular 31.8%, ratio 1.26×)
sched_j_main.housing_allowance_residence (structurally elevated due to §107 — not a behavioral signal)
sched_j_main contingent-comp (per-filing 0.0625% vs secular 0.491%, secular is ~7.9× religion — theological constraint hypothesis)
sched_j_main any-row (per-filing 9.23%, ranks #24 of 24 — lowest in dataset; Health Care leads at 55.65%)
§512(b)(13) controlled (conditional 31.2% vs secular 39.3%, religion is BELOW secular by 0.79×)
X.selection_caveat: The single most important caveat in the entire tool: 88,660 filings at 18,017 EINs is the voluntary-filer subset. The non-filing church universe (~126k entities classified NTEE-X in the IRS BMF) is invisible. Any rate here is filer-vs-filer, not population-vs-population.

B.label: Education
B.what_this_sector_is: K-12 private schools, charter schools, universities, vocational schools, parent-teacher orgs, educational support orgs, alumni associations, scholarship funds. 185,568 filings (2014-2024); largest secular major.
B.typical_related_party_profile: Endowment-investment partnerships drive related-entity counts; campus-housing loans for faculty/staff drive insider-loan disclosure (3.55%); alumni-affiliated foundations drive Sched R Pt II rate to 20.91%; professionalized comp governance at universities (Sched J Pt I 26.77%), weaker at small private schools.
B.comparison_to_religion: Strong structural parallels with religion on housing benefits (campus housing vs parsonage) and founder-dependence at the small end (founder-led private schools). Universities operate under much stricter procedural governance than even the most professionalized religious orgs.
fields_where_this_sector_is_notable: sched_r_transactions Pt V (12.82% — endowment-investment and alumni-foundation transfers)
sched_j_main any-row (26.77% — university executive comp governance)

E.label: Health Care
E.what_this_sector_is: Hospitals, health systems, physician practices, community health centers, hospices, ambulatory surgery centers. 96,633 filings (2014-2024). Includes religiously-sponsored hospitals (Catholic, Adventist, Baptist, Mennonite, Jewish systems) which are coded E, not X.
E.typical_related_party_profile: The most related-party-dense sector in the dataset. Physician-practice subsidiaries, foundation fundraising affiliates, system holding-company architecture, captive insurance subsidiaries, and joint-venture surgery centers all populate Sched R heavily. Leads on Pt IV (11.38%), Sched R Pt V (26.52%), Sched J Pt I any-row (55.65%), Sched R Pt II (48.60%).
E.comparison_to_religion: Religiously-sponsored health systems are statistically in Health Care, not in religion. This is the most consequential coding boundary affecting religious-vs-secular comparison. The 'religion is lower than Health Care on every Health Care-dense field' headline is partly an artifact of NTEE classification.
fields_where_this_sector_is_notable: sched_l_business_transactions Pt IV (11.38% — physician-vendor relationships, leads dataset)
sched_j_main any-row (55.65% — leads dataset; professionalized executive comp governance)
sched_j_compensation.total_filing_org (top of executive comp distribution per regulatory framing)

F.label: Mental Health & Crisis
F.what_this_sector_is: Community mental-health centers, crisis-intervention services, substance-use treatment, counseling centers, suicide-prevention orgs. 28,772 filings (2014-2024) — 29,726 with partial-2025.
F.typical_related_party_profile: Smaller orgs, founder-led at the small end, less professionalized comp governance. The only secular major where §4958 excess-benefit admission rate (0.1112%, 32 of 28,772) exceeds religion's (0.0578%). F is the leader on §4958 in the 24-major leaderboard.
F.comparison_to_religion: Structurally similar to small religious orgs in founder-dependence, small board size, weaker procedural governance. The elevated §4958 rate suggests this structural pattern (not religion specifically) is the underlying risk driver. F is now established as the leader on §4958 above religion under the post-audit denominator.

P.label: Human Services
P.what_this_sector_is: Direct-service social-welfare orgs: food banks, homeless shelters (overlaps L), family services, child welfare, youth services, immigration services, adult day care, etc. Heavy faith-affiliated subset (Catholic Charities, Lutheran Services, Jewish Family Service, Salvation Army affiliates). 171,347 filings (2014-2024); second-largest sector.
P.typical_related_party_profile: Federation-affiliated org structures drive Sched R Pt II rates (19.35%); government-contract revenue drives Pt IV business transactions (6.38%); §4958 disclosure rate 0.0286% (49 of 171,347) is roughly half religion's; professionalized comp governance at large federated orgs, weaker at small community-based orgs.
P.comparison_to_religion: The most overlapping sector with religion in social positioning. The faith-affiliated service subset of P shares organizational DNA with X but is coded for primary activity (social services), not for religious affiliation. Direct X-vs-P comparison conflates 'pastoral' (X) vs 'faith-affiliated service' (P).
fields_where_this_sector_is_notable: sched_j_main any-row (21.96% — professionalized at large orgs)

T.label: Philanthropy & Voluntarism
T.what_this_sector_is: Public-charity foundations (vs 990-PF private foundations), donor-advised-fund sponsors, federated giving (United Way affiliates), community foundations, alumni foundations, supporting-org grantmakers. 58,410 filings (2014-2024).
T.typical_related_party_profile: Highest 509(a)(3) supporting-org density among secular sectors per regulatory framing; foundation-affiliate architecture drives Sched R Pt II to 29.03%; controlled-entity status common; Pt V transaction volume high (15.85%) because grantmaking to affiliated operating entities is the core business.
T.comparison_to_religion: T's foundation-architecture maps closely to religion's denominational-endowment and missionary-fund subset. Direct comparison captures the 509(a)(3) governance regime as much as the religious/secular distinction.
fields_where_this_sector_is_notable: sched_r_related_tax_exempt Pt II (29.03% — foundation-affiliate density, ranks #4 of 24)
sched_r_transactions Pt V (15.85% — heavy grant-to-affiliate flow)

L.label: Housing & Shelter
L.what_this_sector_is: Affordable-housing developers (LIHTC), homeless-shelter operators, transitional-housing programs, public-housing-affiliate orgs, senior housing. 77,132 filings (2014-2024).
L.typical_related_party_profile: Each property typically held in a separate LLC for liability/financing reasons. Highest Sched R Pt II rate (52.18%) in the dataset — entirely structural for tax-credit and lender requirements. High Sched R Pt V at 20.80%. Low Sched L Pt I at 0.0052% (lowest of the substantial majors) and lowest insider-loan rate (2.02%).
L.comparison_to_religion: The clearest example of why disclosure-density is not fraud-density. L's structural use of related-LLC architecture inflates every Sched R rate without any fraud-relevant signal.
fields_where_this_sector_is_notable: sched_r_related_tax_exempt Pt II (52.18% — leads dataset; LIHTC architecture)
sched_j_main any-row (32.44% — institutionalized housing-system executive comp)

S.label: Community Improvement
S.what_this_sector_is: Chambers of commerce, business-improvement districts, neighborhood associations, community development corps, economic-development orgs. 78,731 filings (2014-2024).
S.typical_related_party_profile: Heavy 501(c)(4)/(c)(6) co-presence in related entities (business-association ecosystem) per regulatory framing. Low Sched L Pt I rate (0.0102%, 8 of 78,731) makes S a useful 'low-baseline' comparator. Religion at 0.0578% is ~5.7× S.
S.comparison_to_religion: Different ecosystem from religion (business-association rather than religious-community). Useful as a low-baseline secular benchmark for excess-benefit rates.
fields_where_this_sector_is_notable: sched_l_excess_benefit (0.0102% — among the lowest, useful low-baseline)

Q.label: International, Foreign Affairs
Q.what_this_sector_is: International development, foreign mission organizations (including faith-based), humanitarian relief, international policy/advocacy, exchange programs. 32,910 filings (2014-2024).
Q.typical_related_party_profile: Most foreign-domicile activity in the dataset per regulatory framing; most legitimate offshore-affiliate use. Faith-based foreign missions (Samaritan's Purse, World Vision US, Compassion International, etc.) are coded Q, not X. Sched L Pt I 0.0365% (ranks #6 of 24).
Q.comparison_to_religion: Q captures a large fraction of what the public would call 'religious international work' — the NTEE coding boundary moves it out of religion. Direct X-vs-Q comparison helps separate 'religion' from 'foreign mission.'

A.label: Arts, Culture & Humanities
A.what_this_sector_is: Museums, performing arts, visual arts, humanities orgs, historical societies, media (non-religious), libraries. 108,296 filings (2014-2024); third-largest sector.
A.typical_related_party_profile: Highest insider-loan rate in dataset (4.89%) — per regulatory framing driven by donor-founder bankrolling (loan_to_organization direction); founder-passion orgs common at small end; donor-board members common. Sched L Pt I 0.0342% (ranks #7 of 24).
A.comparison_to_religion: Resembles religion in founder-passion structure; insider-loan rates near-tied (A 4.89%, X 4.70%). Loan direction is the hypothesized differentiator — Arts is more often donor-funds-org, religion is more often org-funds-pastor — though the split is not numerically confirmed in current data.

subgroup_framing.boring_sectors_note: NTEE majors that are not worth dedicated comparison framing in the religion-vs-secular tool: D Animal-related (32,899 filings; small, structurally bland), G Voluntary Health Associations (18,011; specialty disease orgs, narrow signal), H Medical Research (8,982; very small, distinct regime — but #3 on §4958 at 0.0445%), I Crime & Legal-Related (18,434; specialized, low signal), J Employment (20,482; small, structurally bland), K Food/Agriculture (17,216; small, low signal), M Public Safety (34,266; lowest rates on most fraud-relevant fields, but for boring structural reasons — volunteer fire departments), N Recreation & Sports (71,059; athletic-club-like pattern), O Youth Development (31,727; mid-pack on everything), R Civil Rights & Civic Action (10,240; small, advocacy-bias profile), U Science & Tech (6,582; small, high org-size variance), V Social Science (2,755; smallest major, insufficient cells for stable rates — zero §4958 disclosures), W Public & Societal Benefit (18,534; catch-all).

global_caveats.headline: Disclosure is not wrongdoing
global_caveats.body: Every rate in this tool is a disclosure rate. A high rate can mean more wrongdoing, more conscientious reporting, or more complex related-party architecture for non-fraud reasons. Schedule R is the clearest example: Housing & Shelter has the highest Sched R rates because affordable-housing developers structurally hold each property in a separate LLC — not because Housing has more fraud. Always ask what the structural baseline is before reading rate elevation as fraud signal.

global_caveats.headline: Two rate constructions are in use; do not mix them
global_caveats.body: Every per-filing rate in this tool uses n_distinct_filings_with_at_least_one_row / n_canonical_filings (the disclose-rate construction). The alternative n_rows / n_filings construction over-weights orgs that disclose many rows in one filing and is NOT used as a rate. Conditional rates (in-default loans, unwritten loans, §512(b)(13) controlled, sentinel names) use a different denominator (rows in the relevant table) and are explicitly tagged rate_kind=conditional in rel_vs_sec.json. Per-filing rates and conditional rates cannot be placed on the same axis without explicit segregation.

global_caveats.headline: Headline rates are 2014-2024, excluding partial 2025
global_caveats.body: Snapshot date is 2026-05-24. 2025 is a partial cohort (~14% of a full year by row count). Every headline ratio in this file uses 2014-2024. The with_2025 versions are computed and carried alongside in rel_vs_sec.json for transparency but are not the headline. Treat any number you can't trace to 2014-2024 as suspect.

global_caveats.headline: Church-exemption hole shapes the religion corpus
global_caveats.body: IRC §6033(a)(3)(A)(i) exempts churches from filing Form 990. The 17,870 EINs (2014-2024) / 18,017 EINs (incl 2025) in the religion corpus are the voluntary-filer subset: ECFA members, federal-grant recipients under the Single Audit Act, religious-school operators, and religious orgs that chose to file. The non-filing church universe (~126,000 entities classified NTEE-X in the IRS Business Master File) is invisible. Every comparison ratio is filer-vs-filer, not population-vs-population. The voluntary-filer subset is more accountability-minded than the non-filing universe on average, so the visible religion rates are likely an OPTIMISTIC lower bound on what the full population would show on most procedural-governance fields.

global_caveats.headline: Group-ruling subordinates excluded from both corpora
global_caveats.body: Rev. Proc. 80-27 (updated by Rev. Proc. 2018-40) lets a central organization file a single coordinated return covering subordinate entities. This excludes most US Catholic dioceses, parishes, schools and affiliates; most Southern Baptist Convention affiliates; most United Methodist Church / ELCA conference structures. The IRS 990 dataset — and therefore this tool — systematically under-represents Catholic, mainline Protestant, and large-denominational activity. Independent and non-denominational religious orgs are over-represented.

global_caveats.headline: NTEE coding is an IRS classification, not a religious self-identification
global_caveats.body: NTEE-X captures orgs the IRS coded as religious in the Business Master File. Religiously-sponsored hospitals are NTEE-E (Health Care), faith-based foreign missions are typically NTEE-Q (International), faith-affiliated social services are typically NTEE-P (Human Services). The X-vs-secular comparison is therefore pastoral / theologically-primary religion vs everything else — not religious activity vs non-religious activity. Three of the four largest comparisons (X vs E, X vs P, X vs Q) are affected by this boundary.

global_caveats.headline: No external fraud-label join
global_caveats.body: This tool does not join 990 disclosures to SEC enforcement actions, DOJ indictments, state-AG actions, or charity-watchdog ratings. The 990 disclosures are themselves the signal: §4958 admissions, unwritten insider-loan terms, in-default loans, sentinel counterparty names, contingent comp, §512(b)(13)-controlled entities. Whether a given org is also subject to external enforcement is a separate inquiry.

global_caveats.headline: 2019 trough is COVID, not behavior
global_caveats.body: Every related-party table shows a ~45% volume trough at tax-period-end 2019. Those filings actually landed in calendar 2020 under IRS extension orders; the tax_period field stamps them as 2019. Treat 2019 as not-a-comparable-year in any time-series comparison.

global_caveats.headline: Sentinel filter is the extended post-audit version
global_caveats.body: The religion-tuned sentinel filter (SUBSTANTIAL CONTRIBUTOR, NONE, VARIOUS, BOARD MEMBER, OFFICER, etc.) missed the secular corpus's dominant role-placeholders. The extended list (post-audit, 2026-05) now also catches VACANT, OPEN, POSITION OPEN, TBD, TBA, VOLUNTEER, RESIGNED, FORMER, RETIRED, DECEASED, INTERIM, ACTING, SEE ABOVE, SEE ATTACHED, AS NEEDED, NOT APPLICABLE, NOT REQUIRED, UNKNOWN, BOARD OF DIRECTORS, plus single-word common role/surname stand-ins (PRESIDENT, EXECUTIVE, MANAGER, FOUNDER) and short all-letter initials (≤3 chars). Religion sentinel rate (conditional, 2014-2024): 6.10% (910 of 14,921 Sched L rows). Secular: 9.25% (18,738 of 202,511). VACANT alone was #1 in the pre-audit pt_vii_people.json at 344 EINs.

global_caveats.headline: Rebuttable-presumption procedural fields not extractable
global_caveats.body: Reg. §53.4958-6 requires three elements for the rebuttable presumption of comp reasonableness: independent body approval, comparability data, contemporaneous documentation. The Form 990 Pt VI L15 trio that historically captured this is schema-deprecated from 2014v5.0+ and now lives in Sched O free text. The Sched J Pt I fields that approximate it (compensation_committee, compensation_survey) are populated; independent_compensation_consultant, written_policy_for_above, and approval_by_board_or_comp_committee are empty in the parsed corpus. The dataset cannot reconstruct full rebuttable-presumption posture.

global_caveats.headline: Small NTEE majors have unstable rates
global_caveats.body: Social Science (V, 2,755 filings 2014-2024), Science & Technology (U, 6,582), Medical Research (H, 8,982), and Civil Rights & Civic Action (R, 10,240) have small enough cell sizes that subgroup rates on low-base-rate fields like sched_l_excess_benefit are statistically noisy. Require n_filings ≥ ~15,000 and n_with_disclosure ≥ ~30 for stable rate estimation on the rarer fields. V has zero §4958 disclosures across the entire 2014-2024 window.

global_caveats.headline: Form 990 (full) only — 990-EZ and 990-PF excluded
global_caveats.body: 990-EZ filers don't file Sched L Pt IV or Sched R; 990-PF private foundations operate under the different §4941 self-dealing regime. The corpus therefore excludes small public charities (revenue typically <$200k) and private foundations. The visible related-party landscape is biased toward larger nonprofits.

global_caveats.headline: §4958 admissions are a floor, not a population
global_caveats.body: Schedule L Part I is a self-incrimination box. Reporting a non-zero entry is a tax admission triggering 25% first-tier excise tax on the disqualified person and 10% manager tax on knowing approvers. Filers do not volunteer these entries. In the religion corpus (2014-2024 excl partial-2025): 50 canonical filings with at least one Pt I row, at 27 distinct EINs, 84 raw rows. In the secular corpus over the same window: 307 canonical filings at 203 EINs, 446 raw rows. The disclosed floor — not an estimate of the actual excess-benefit population.
